## Objective
- Expand and improve the existing game: make it more realistic, add more players, a larger map, and more guns.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing playable game; do not ask clarifying questions.
- Make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- Turned the single-enemy scenario into a larger station encounter with three hostiles and four wandering crew.
- Expanded the map from 17×13 to 27×19, added four evidence terminals, and added three selectable weapons: pistol, rifle, and shotgun.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reworked `game.js` for the larger station, multiple crew and hostiles, four objectives, weapon switching, ammo/reloading, and revised combat.
- Updated the start screen and HUD defaults in `index.html`.
- `node --check game.js` passed before the latest small fixes.

### Active
- Finish the weapon HUD’s tap-to-cycle interaction and its visual hint; validate the updated game in-browser and check for gameplay bugs.
- Run syntax/status checks after the latest edits.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add a click/tap handler on `.weapon` to cycle weapons and update the hint styling/text as needed.
2. Update the stale `#help-hint` text in `index.html` to mention weapon selection.
3. Run `node --check game.js`, inspect the final diff, and launch the game for a quick browser smoke test.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Core gameplay, station map, NPCs, combat, weapons, and HUD updates.
- `index.html`: HUD and start-screen copy; still has a stale help hint to update.
- `style.css`: Existing HUD and responsive styling; consider adding a clear tap-to-cycle affordance.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `game.js` was rewritten and patched; syntax passed once before fixes to angle normalization, weapon icon selection, and raycasting from arbitrary origins.
- The tap-to-cycle interaction has not yet been implemented, though the weapon HUD title says “Tap to switch weapons.”

## Objective
- Expand and improve the existing playable game with more realism, players, map area, and guns.

## Requirements
- Build on the existing game without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them on completion.

## Decisions
- Turned the single-enemy scenario into a station encounter with three hostiles and four wandering crew.
- Expanded the map to 27×19, added four evidence terminals, and added pistol, rifle, and shotgun loadouts.

## Work State
### Completed
- Reworked gameplay for the larger station, NPCs, objectives, weapons, ammo/reloading, and combat.
- Updated the start screen and HUD for the new scenario.
- Added weapon cycling by number keys, mouse wheel, and tapping/clicking the weapon HUD; updated its visual and accessibility affordances.
- Updated the stale help hint and fixed the weapon HUD’s ammo-caption selector.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Validate gameplay in a browser and inspect for remaining runtime or gameplay bugs.

### Blocked
- Browser smoke test: `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` failed because Playwright’s Chromium is not installed (`Browser "chromium" is not installed`).

## Next Move
1. Install or configure a browser for Playwright, then smoke-test the start screen, weapon switching, and gameplay.
2. Review the final diff and report completion; changes remain uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: map, NPCs, combat, weapons, HUD, and interaction logic.
- `index.html`: HUD, controls, and start-screen copy.
- `style.css`: HUD and weapon-card affordances.

## Important Context
- A local HTTP server was started on port 3002 for browser testing.
- `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css` have uncommitted changes.
